archetypes.name: allow-list-coverage
archetypes.rationale: Static reviewers check logic and test coverage but won't grep callers to verify that the 11 new allow-list entries have real launch sites, or that launch-claude-subprocess.sh actually emits OK/ERROR/TIMEOUT rather than already-normalized values.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine whether the 11 new task kinds added to `scripts/lib-timing-kinds.sh` (e.g. `claude-review`, `scout-dynamic-archetypes`, `claude-phase3-aggregator`) correspond to actual call sites in `skills/`, `scripts/launch-*`, or related launchers. Verify that `launch-claude-subprocess.sh` actually emits the `OK`, `ERROR`, and `TIMEOUT` status aliases that `timing-ledger.sh` now normalizes, rather than already-normalized `complete`/`signal` values. Check whether any documentation or comments outside the changed files still reference the old constraint (`vendor claude is only supported for task-kind claude-ci-fix`) and therefore describe now-stale behavior. Confirm that the status normalization (`OK`→`complete`, `ERROR`/`TIMEOUT`→`signal`) applies only when the vendor check already passed, so a bad vendor cannot trigger normalization side-effects. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
